body.statement: The interval \(I_{T,\Delta}\) is \(O_{T,\Delta}\)-measurable and uniformly honest over \(\mathfrak M_T(\alpha,\beta,L,c,C,\varepsilon)\cup\mathfrak M_T^{\mathrm{low}}(\alpha,\beta,L,c,\varepsilon)\) without conditioning on \(E_T\) and without convergence of \(t^\alpha\pi_t(1)\). Measurability follows from the recorded calendar revelation times: main-prefix and old-prefix age-window indicators are known at \(H_T\), including when a response remains unrevealed. On \(\mathfrak M_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm{reg}}(\kappa)\), \(\sup_x|P\{(\widehat\tau_{T,\Delta}-\tau+b_{T,\Delta})/\widehat s_{T,\Delta}\leq x\}-\Phi(x)|\to0\) and \(\widehat s_{T,\Delta}/s_{T,\Delta}\to1\) uniformly. If the gate fails, \(I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm{conc}}\) retains coverage; if it passes, \(I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm G}\) has the bounded-shift Gaussian coverage envelope, including triangular arrays with variance approaching the threshold \(1/\log T\).
body.justification: This is the load-bearing uniform studentization result that makes one implementable procedure valid in both Gaussian and degenerate regimes.
body.gap: Bibaut et al., Hadad et al., and Shi, Wang, and Wu rely on centered scores plus variance consistency or convergence; none treats an outcome-selected reveal process with an overlapping correction and an observable low-variance splice.
body.consumer: The theorem yields a prespecifiable implementation that does not fail when the inferior-arm outcome variance is small or the adaptive allocation oscillates.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(K_a=K_a(n_T)\), \(J_a=K_a(k_T)\), \(\sigma_a^2=\operatorname{Var}_P(X_{a,1}^{\Delta})\), and
\[
 Z_T=(M_{1,\Delta}-PM_{1,\Delta})-(M_{0,\Delta}-PM_{0,\Delta}),
 \qquad
 C_T=(U_{1,\Delta}-PU_{1,\Delta})-(U_{0,\Delta}-PU_{0,\Delta}).
\]
On \(E_T\), lem:old-cohort-correction gives the exact decomposition
\[
 \widehat\tau_{T,\Delta}-\tau+b_{T,\Delta}=Z_T+C_T. \tag{1}
\]

\emph{Measurability.}
On \(E_T\), the first \(K_a\) assignments to arm \(a\) occur by \(n_T\), hence have age at least \(H_T-n_T=g_{T,\Delta}\) at the terminal time.  The first \(J_a\) occur by \(k_T\), hence have age at least \(H_T-k_T=h_{T,\Delta}\).  A record revealed by those ages supplies its outcome and delay; absence of a revelation by the corresponding age makes the relevant truncated indicator zero.  Thus every \(X_{a,j}^{\Delta}\), \(R_{a,j}^{\Delta}\), sample variance, gate, and interval endpoint is a measurable function of \(O_{T,\Delta}\).  The conventions on \(E_T^c\) are measurable as well.

\emph{The concentration branch.}
For independent centered variables in an interval of length \(2\), convexity of the exponential gives
\[
 P\{|Z_T|\geq\sqrt{2S_Tx}\}\leq2e^{-x},
 \qquad S_T=K_1^{-1}+K_0^{-1}. \tag{2}
\]
For completeness, this follows by applying
\(P\exp\{\lambda(X-PX)\}\leq\exp(\lambda^2/2)\)
to each weighted tape variable and optimizing over \(\lambda\).
For a centered \(R\), \(|R-PR|\leq2\) and
\(P(R-PR)^2\leq PR^2\leq v_{T,\Delta}\).  Expanding its exponential series and using
\(|R-PR|^j\leq2^{j-2}(R-PR)^2\), \(j\geq2\), gives, after exponential Markov optimization,
\[
 P\!\left\{|U_{a,\Delta}-PU_{a,\Delta}|
 >\sqrt{\frac{2v_{T,\Delta}x}{J_a}}+\frac{4x}{3J_a}\right\}
 \leq2e^{-x}. \tag{3}
\]
With \(x=x_\eta=\log(6/\eta)\), (2), the two bounds (3), and a union bound have total failure probability at most \(\eta\).  On their joint complement, (1) and \(|b_{T,\Delta}|\leq B_{T,\Delta}\) imply
\(\tau\in I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm{conc}}\).  Intersecting with \([-2,2]\) cannot remove \(\tau\).  Since the actual interval is \([-2,2]\) on \(E_T^c\), this argument is unconditional: the deviation event is defined on the complete tapes, and no conditioning on \(E_T\) occurs.

\emph{Uniform Gaussian approximation above the variance threshold.}
Define
\[
 V_T=\sigma_1^2+\mathbf 1\{\alpha=0\}\sigma_0^2.
\]
Consider first the triangular-array regime \(V_T\geq1/\log T\).  If \(\alpha>0\), then
\[
 s_{T,\Delta}^2\geq\frac{1}{K_1\log T};
\]
if \(\alpha=0\), comparability of \(K_0\) and \(K_1\) gives
\[
 s_{T,\Delta}^2\geq \frac{c_0}{T\log T}
\]
for a fixed \(c_0>0\).  The largest absolute summand of \(Z_T/s_{T,\Delta}\) is consequently
\[
 O\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log T}{K_1}}\right)=o(1)
\]
for \(\alpha>0\), and \(O(\sqrt{\log T/T})=o(1)\) for \(\alpha=0\).  The normalized summands are independent, centered, bounded, and their variances sum to one.

Here is a direct triangular-array argument.  If \(\xi_{Tj}\) are those normalized summands and
\(\delta_T=\max_j|\xi_{Tj}|\), Taylor's formula gives, for each fixed \(t\),
\[
 \prod_jP e^{it\xi_{Tj}}
 =\exp\!\left\{-\frac{t^2}{2}
 +O\!\left(|t|^3\delta_T\sum_jP\xi_{Tj}^2
 +t^4\sum_j(P\xi_{Tj}^2)^2\right)\right\}
 \longrightarrow e^{-t^2/2}. \tag{4}
\]
Indeed \(\sum_j(P\xi_{Tj}^2)^2\leq\delta_T^2\).
Tightness follows from the unit variance.  Every weakly convergent subsequence has, by (4), Gaussian characteristic function, which uniquely determines \(N(0,1)\).  Thus \(Z_T/s_{T,\Delta}\Rightarrow N(0,1)\).  The bounds on \(\delta_T\) are uniform, so a contradiction-subsequence argument and continuity of \(\Phi\) strengthen this to
\[
 \sup_{P,\Pi}\sup_x
 \left|P\{Z_T/s_{T,\Delta}\leq x\}-\Phi(x)\right|\longrightarrow0 \tag{5}
\]
over the stated high-variance regime.

The correction is negligible there.  Lem:old-cohort-correction and the lower bound for \(s_{T,\Delta}^2\) yield
\[
 \frac{P C_T^2}{s_{T,\Delta}^2}
 \leq
 C(\log T)T^{1-\alpha-\rho(\beta+1-\alpha)}
 \longrightarrow0. \tag{6}
\]
For sample variances, with \(K\geq2\),
\[
 \widehat\sigma^2=\frac{K}{K-1}\{\overline{X^2}-\bar X^2\}.
\]
Since \(|X|\leq1\), Chebyshev applied to \(\overline{X^2}\) and \(\bar X\) gives
\[
 \widehat\sigma_a^2-\sigma_a^2=O_P(K_a^{-1/2}) \tag{7}
\]
uniformly.  When \(\alpha>0\), divide the arm-one term in (7) by
\(\sigma_1^2\geq1/\log T\); the arm-zero weighted error is bounded, relative to \(s_{T,\Delta}^2\), by
\[
 O_P\!\left(\frac{K_1\log T}{K_0^{3/2}}\right)=o_P(1).
\]
When \(\alpha=0\), the two \(K_a\)'s are comparable to \(T\), and division by
\(\sigma_1^2+\sigma_0^2\geq1/\log T\) gives the same conclusion.  Hence
\[
 \widehat s_{T,\Delta}/s_{T,\Delta}\longrightarrow1 \tag{8}
\]
uniformly in the high-variance regime.  Equations (1), (5), (6), and (8), together with \(P(E_T^c)\to0\), prove the asserted studentized approximation there, with any measurable extension of the displayed quotient on \(E_T^c\).

On the regular class, truncation does not destroy the variance floor.  Indeed, if
\(X=Y\mathbf 1\{D\leq g_{T,\Delta}\}\), then
\[
 |\operatorname{Var}(X)-\operatorname{Var}(Y)|
 \leq |P(X^2-Y^2)|+|(PX)^2-(PY)^2|
 \leq3P\{D>g_{T,\Delta}\}\leq3v_{T,\Delta}. \tag{9}
\]
Thus ass:regular-variance and \(v_{T,\Delta}\to0\) imply \(V_T\geq\kappa/2\) eventually (with an immaterial adjustment of the constant when \(\alpha=0\)).  This places the whole regular class in the regime of (5)--(8) and proves both uniform assertions in the theorem, without any convergence requirement on \(t^\alpha\pi_t(1)\).

\emph{The gate and bounded-shift coverage.}
For \(B\geq0\) define \(f_B(s)=s\,c_\eta(B/s)\), \(s>0\).  If \(Z\sim N(0,1)\), then
\[
 P\{|sZ-b|\leq f_B(s)\}
 =\Phi(c_\eta(B/s)+b/s)+\Phi(c_\eta(B/s)-b/s)-1
 \geq1-\eta \tag{10}
\]
for every \(|b|\leq B\), because the last expression decreases with \(|b|\) and the defining equation for \(c_\eta\) is equality at \(|b|=B\).
Let \(z_\gamma=\Phi^{-1}(\gamma)\).  The defining equation also gives
\[
 B+z_{1-\eta}s\leq f_B(s)\leq B+z_{1-\eta/2}s. \tag{11}
\]
Moreover \(f_B\) is uniformly Lipschitz in \(s\), with a constant depending only on \(\eta\).  To see this, write \(u=B/s\), \(x=c_\eta(u)-u\).  Then
\[
 z_{1-\eta}\leq x\leq z_{1-\eta/2},\qquad
 0\leq c_\eta'(u)
 =\frac{\phi(c_\eta(u)-u)-\phi(c_\eta(u)+u)}
 {\phi(c_\eta(u)-u)+\phi(c_\eta(u)+u)}
 \leq1.
\]
Hence
\[
 f_B'(s)=x+\frac{2u\phi(x+2u)}{\phi(x)+\phi(x+2u)}
\]
is bounded uniformly over \(B,u,s\).  Therefore (5)--(8), (10), and a deterministic-endpoint sandwich imply that \(I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm G}\) has coverage at least \(1-\eta-o(1)\) throughout \(V_T\geq1/\log T\).  The extra radius \(d_{T,\Delta}\) can only increase coverage; from the quota orders and the choice of \(\rho\),
\[
 d_{T,\Delta}
 =O\!\left(
 \sqrt{T^{-\rho(\beta+1-\alpha)}\log T}
 +T^{-\rho(1-\alpha)}\log T\right)
 =o(T^{-q}). \tag{12}
\]
This includes arrays with \(V_T\) of order \(1/\log T\).

It remains to verify that data-dependent splicing does not spend the error probability twice.  If \(V_T\leq1/\log T\), (7) and Chebyshev imply
\[
 \sup_{P,\Pi}P(G_{T,\Delta})\longrightarrow0, \tag{13}
\]
because the gate is separated from \(V_T\) by \(1/\log T\) and
\((\log T)^2/K_1\to0\).  The concentration branch then gives coverage
\(1-\eta-o(1)\).
If \(V_T>1/\log T\), use Gaussian coverage.  On \(G_{T,\Delta}^c\), the bounded empirical variance and the gate imply
\[
 \widehat s_{T,\Delta}=o(T^{-q})
\]
deterministically: for \(\alpha>0\),
\(\widehat s^2\leq2/(K_1\log T)+2/K_0\), and for \(\alpha=0\),
\(\widehat s^2=O(1/(T\log T))\).
By (11), (12), and
\(a_T=\sqrt{2S_Tx_\eta}\asymp T^{-q}\),
\[
 f_{B_{T,\Delta}}(\widehat s_{T,\Delta})+d_{T,\Delta}
 \leq B_{T,\Delta}+o(a_T)
 \leq B_{T,\Delta}+a_T+A_{1,T,\Delta}(x_\eta)+A_{0,T,\Delta}(x_\eta)
\]
for all sufficiently large \(T\).  Thus \(I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm{conc}}\) contains
\(I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm G}\) on gate failure.  The selected interval consequently contains the Gaussian interval throughout the high-variance regime, while (13) makes its Gaussian selection negligible in the low-variance regime.  Combining the two cases, and recalling that quota failure returns the full parameter interval, proves uniform honesty over the union of model classes.  It also establishes exactly the claimed observable variance-gate and fallback behavior.
